doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Billy Cobham's 51-piece kit and Roy Brooks's toy drummers
summary: Fuller recalls Art Blakey mocking Billy Cobham's giant kit, and Brower recalls Brooks's toy-drummer show; Brooks later in an asylum.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Freddie Bridgette. You call him something else, what do you call him?
Drums. He was never a real bona fide drummer you know? I mean, for me, it’s kind of limited in the drum department. There are only a few that I really…
Yeah, a percussionist. You know like Billy used to play with the… The New York… Do you remember Hubert Laws and all those guys?
He played with Horace for a while, and he had 51 pieces, and Art Blakey used to come in and say--

Billy Cobham. Art Blakey said, “ 51 pieces are you kidding!? You can’t hit that little joint, you have to get up off the stool and walk around in front of it to hit it!” He said, “why don’t you learn how to play the three drums that are there?” Hana was wanting to talk, he was always going up to the microphone saying, “in this particular arrangement I play the polyphonic…” Boy it was funny!

One Time I saw Brooks and he had these toy drummers, he had all these toys drummers. In some kind of way he could… He had this laser thing that he could trigger them with. You know when the Chinese had like the – – he had like an army of toy drummers in some kind of a way he was triggering the shit. He was out there.
He was out there! You know where he is now, or where he was?
